issue: Does a conviction for conspiracy or attempt to commit a drug offense qualify as a 'controlled substance offense' under U.S.S.G. § 4B1.2(b), given that Application Note 1 includes inchoate offenses in that definition?

sides.position: Inchoate offenses such as conspiracy and attempt qualify as controlled substance offenses under § 4B1.2(b), and Application Note 1 is consistent with the Guidelines text.
cases: United States v. Mao, No. 24-2107 (1st Cir. 2026)
United States v. Gerrish, 96 F.4th 67 (1st Cir. 2024)
United States v. Richardson, 958 F.3d 151 (2d Cir. 2020)
United States v. Vargas, 74 F.4th 673 (5th Cir. 2023) (en banc)
United States v. Maloid, 71 F.4th 795 (10th Cir. 2023)

sides.position: Inchoate offenses such as conspiracy and attempt do not qualify as controlled substance offenses under § 4B1.2(b), because the Application Note's inclusion of them is inconsistent with the guideline text.
cases: United States v. Campbell, 22 F.4th 438 (4th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Dupree, 57 F.4th 1269 (11th Cir. 2023) (en banc)

this_court: Inchoate offenses qualify as controlled substance offenses under § 4B1.2(b); the court adheres to its precedent on Application Note 1 and declines to resolve the split in the defendant's favor.
quote: we decline Mao's invitation to further entrench the circuit split on this issue.
cite: United States v. Mao, No. 24-2107 (1st Cir. 2026)
